Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zagabishije Madagascar ku bijanye no gukomeza ubucuti ifitaniye n'Uburusiya, zivuga ko ugukorana nk'ukwo intwaro z'abasirikare zagiranye n'Uburusiya mu bihugu vyo muri Afrika y'Uburengero kutashoboye gutuma umutekano utera imbere.

Icegera c'umuyobozi ajejwe ibikorwa vy'igisirikare ca Amerika muri Afrika, Lt Gen John Brennan, yavuze ko kuba Madagascar iherereye mu karere k'ibahari Indiyano bituma igira uruhara rukomeye mu bijanye n'urudandaza mpuzamakungu.

Yagabishije ico gihugu kudakurikiza "uburorero bwo muri Sahel", avuga ko bushobora gutuma umutekano muke urushiriza gukwira ku mugabane wa Afrika.

Ibihugu vya Mali, Burkina Faso na Niger, vyose birongowe n'abasirikare, vyarahagaritse ubucuti bwavyo n'ibihugu vyo mu Burengero, bihitamwo kwitura Uburusiya kugira ngo bubifashe mu vya gisirikare mu rugamba birimwo rwo kurwanya imihari y'abajihadiste.

Uburusiya bwaraguye imigenderanire mu vya gisirikare na Madagascar kuva abasirikare bafashe ubutegetsi muri ico gihugu mu 2025. Buyirungikira ibirwanisho hamwe n'abamenyereza mu vya gisirikare.

Mu kiganiro n'abamenyeshamakuru biciye kuri internet, Brennan yagize ati: "Turatewe umutima uhagaze n'ukuntu Uburusiya bushaka gukwiragiza akarorero ko muri Sahel mu bindi bice vy'umugabane wa Afrika".

Yabandanije ati: « Madagascar iherereye ahantu hahambaye cane, co kimwe na Mozambike, rero ntitwipfuza kubona ubwo burorero bukoreshwa muri ivyo bihugu bibiri".

Abategetsi b'ibihugu bitatu vyo mu karere ka Sahel bari babanje kwagiriza ibihugu vyo mu burengero vyahoze ari ibifatanyabikorwa ko bitashoboye guhagarika imihari y'abajihadiste, imbere y'uko bahindukirira Moscou kugira ngo ibifashe.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ariko rero, ibitero vy'iyo mihari vyarabandanije, n'ubwo ivyo bihugu vyongereje ugufashanya n'Uburusiya mu vya gisirikare.

Brennan yagaragaje kandi impungenge zijanye n'umutekano mu muhora wo mu kiyaga ca Mozambike (Mozambique Channel), utandukanya Mozambike na Madagasikari n'umugabane wa Afrika. Uwo muhora ni inzira ihambaye ikoreshwa mu gutwara ibidandazwa hagati y'ibihugu.

Yavuze ko ari ngirakamaro cane gukingira ibikorwa vyo mu mazi, kugira ngo abarwanyi bafitaniye isano n'umuhari wiyita 'reta ya kiislam' mu buraruko bwa Mozambike hamwe n'abandi bashobora guhungabanya umutekano ntibabibangamire.

Afatiye ku biheruka kuba ku nkengera z'ico gihugu bifitaniye isano n'ubusuma bwo mu kiyaga, Brennan yavuze ko imihari y'abarwanyi mu buraruko bwa Mozambike iriko irahindura imikenyuro ikoresha mu bikorwa vy'ubugizi bwa nabi vyayo, harimwo no kurushiriza guteza imbere ubushobozi bwo kugaba ibitero biciye mu mazi.

Yavuze ko abafatanyabikorwa ba Amerika "bafise umwidegemvyo wo gukorana n'abo bashaka", ariko abahimiriza gutahura ingaruka bishobora kugira.

Madagasikari ntaco irashikiriza ku mugaragaro ku majambo ya Brennan.

Perezida Michaël Randrianirina aherutse gusubira gushimangira ko ashigikiye ko ubucuti hagati y'Uburusiya n'ibihugu vya Afrika burushiriza gukomera.

Mu nama y'Uburusiya na Afrika yabaye mu kwezi guheze, Madagasikari n'Uburusiya vyarashize umukono ku masezerano atari make y'ugufashanya mu bijanye n'ukwivuna abansi, ingenzi n'urudandazwa.

Muri Ruhuhuma (2), inyuma y'amezi makeyi afashe ubutegetsi biciye mu guhirika ubutegetsi, Randrianirina yaciye agendera Moscou. Wari umusi wa mbere mu myaka hafi 50 umukuru w'igihugu ca Madagasikari agendeye icese Uburusiya.

MN202611_aq565i15j8.t:
Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson both cost Manchester City more than £100m in the summer

The ongoing international break will give Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca much-needed time to fix the growing issues in his squad.

The Italian made a dream start after taking over from Pep Guardiola in the summer, leading the club to a record seven consecutive victories at the beginning of the Premier League season.

But three consecutive defeats have followed as they have fallen six points adrift of league leaders Arsenal , who are looking in imperious form as they aim to retain their title.

In September, it was announced that City had been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, and matches have continued as the club await the outcome of their appeal.

With possible sanctions hanging over them, is City's recent league form down to psychological issues or are there tactical problems Maresca needs to address?

Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit

Property, football and politics: The links between Manchester and Abu Dhabi explained

Renowned sports psychologist Dr Paul McCarthy has 25 years' experience working in the industry with top clubs in England, Scotland, Germany and France.

McCarthy works on the personal and professional lives of players and says both contribute to how well they perform on the pitch, with the need to "piece together a jigsaw" when situations become disrupted.

"Players are like everyone else - they talk about what is going on in their own lives and things that are topical, especially about uncertain events," McCarthy tells BBC Sport.

"It generates communication with a lot of stories and rumour and over time if there are enough losses, there often becomes a reduced collective efficacy.

"A collective efficacy is a squad's belief in their ability to do what they need to do [to win] and because of their success in the past, that is often shaken a little by consecutive losses."

Man City fan addresses club's midfield problem

City were sitting pretty at the top of the table after a flawless start, but have dropped to third - behind Arsenal and Brighton .

After the guilty verdict was announced during the last international break, Maresca's men won their first game back - against 10-man Liverpool at Anfield - then narrowly overcame Ipswich at Etihad Stadium in their following match.

But they have since lost to Aston Villa , Brighton and Nottingham Forest , with defensive issues exposed and individual mistakes proving costly.

In their first seven games of the season, City did not concede any goals because of individual errors - but that has shifted dramatically in the past three matches, with four mistakes from players contributing to goals.

City have conceded 13 goals after 10 league games - their highest total at this stage of a season since 2008-09, when they had let in 16 - and that has prompted questions about their defensive solidity.

Asked if the uncertainty over the ongoing appeal process may affect the focus and attention of players, McCarthy said: "Yeah, that would be a very reasonable human response.

"When people are uncertain about their future, that uncertainty leads to a lack of perceived control, so uncertainty is often more stressful than bad news and the research shows that.

"So while you are waiting and you don't know the outcome, you are uncertain of where you are and there is that lack of control for a lot of people - they come to training, they play their games and it's outside of their responsibility."

Are Manchester City's players being affected by the charges verdict?

While at Chelsea , in a video for NBC Sports, Maresca discussed his tactics - moving counters into a 3-2-2-3 shape before pushing one up to create the 3-1-6 shape.

He explained using six attackers was a tactic he had employed against Inter Milan to outnumber their back five.

This season, he has adopted the 3-1-6 shape more permanently - trading a second holding midfielder for an extra attacking midfielder.

Coaching a team full of quality footballers, there is logic to wanting to play in a more front-footed and imposing manner, but how well tactics are performed depend on the skillset of the players asked to do them.

City's shape in possession this season has often looked like a 3-1-5-1 or 3-1-6 shape, with Anderson typically the holding midfielder

The big questions come in the form of Elliot Anderson and his midfield partners.

Anderson - naturally more of a roaming midfielder - leans on his physical strengths. At Nottingham Forest , he defended intensely, pressed high and wide, and contributed to attacks. This season, Maresca and his staff have looked to mould him into more of a sitting midfielder after the departure of Rodri in the summer.

Learning that role will take time, as it did for Rodri when he first joined.

It is not problematic in its own right to try to coach a player into a key role, but City have looked exposed through the middle of the pitch more often in recent games.

Anderson, who has largely impressed, has played to his habit - stepping out of a holding midfield position to attempt to press or track opposition players, often looking to win the ball back. Clever opponents have used this to drag him out of position before finding players through the middle.

Enzo Le Fee recognises Anderson's willingness to track him and pulls wide

With Anderson vacating the central area, Brian Brobbey is able to drop in and receive the ball directly from his centre-back

With City looking to press high and often in a man-to-man fashion, Anderson has had to cover more space with his partners in midfield lacking the physicality required to support him.

When City are in possession, Enzo Fernandez - often one of City's midfield three - makes frequent attacking runs off the ball into the final third. When this happens, City can find themselves with as few as two or three players behind the ball, giving opponents favourable conditions to counter-attack if they can break the initial press.

Here, City lose the ball. Anderson is drawn out wide whilst Fernandez on the far side remains high and above the line of the ball, leaving City exposed in the middle

For Maresca, the issue is less around the shape, and more around losing the ball in the first instance. After the loss to Forest, he said: "You concede transitions when you lose the ball, and when you don't win duels."

Further concerns arise when assessing the skillset of the players behind Anderson.

Gianluigi Donnarumma is not a goalkeeper renowned for his ball-playing ability. The defensive cohort are serviceable on the ball but have made costly errors under pressure, playing out from the back, this season too.

City have four players near or behind the ball before Josko Gvardiol is dispossessed. Nottingham Forest, with four attackers of their own, score from this turnover

Guardiola's solution to mitigate some of these issues last season came in the form of asking midfielders to shoulder more ball-playing responsibility.

The loss of Rodri and especially Bernardo Silva, who would drop deep and take City from their own goal into midfield alone, have made City's problems more obvious.

As good as Anderson is, he is not a player who can single-handedly resolve build-up play as Bernardo Silva did, but Ayyoub Bouaddi may be somebody that could be used in this manner as we saw him against Brazil's press in the World Cup.

Long queues formed on key highways as lorries blocked the lanes

Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices.

Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes.

They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran.

Talks between government officials and protest leaders have so far failed to reach a resolution, with another meeting expected to take place on Wednesday.

The protest is being organised by the ⁠Fuerza del Norte trade union, which represents around 80% of Chile's lorry drivers, and the No+TAG civic protest ​movement.

"There is no point of agreement with the government that could offer any perspective to find solutions for everyone," Andrés Alarcón, a spokesman for No+TAG, said after talks broke down on Tuesday, adding "the strike continues".

Economy Minister Daniel Mas called for further dialogue, but warned "at some point, we will have to clear the highways".

He stressed the protests were impacting economic activity and exports, saying "we need to get the country moving again".

The government of President José Antonio Kast has faced public discontent over fuel prices for months.

The average price of diesel has risen 74% since March, according to industry groups.

Juan Cornejo, the president of the Association of Intercity Bus Owners, which represents 14 mid-sized companies, told AFP that "we've reached our limit".

"We've spent more than a month working with negative numbers," he added.

Lorry driver Claudio Elguezabal, who took part in a protest near the capital, Santiago, on Tuesday morning, said the situation was unsustainable.

"Right now I'm not making any profit. Sometimes you even have to put in your own money to cover the client," AFP quoted the 47-year-old as saying.

Dusabimana yavuze ko Umujyi wa Kigali usobanukiwe ko izi nyubako zitunze imiryango myinshi, haba ba nyirazo ndetse n’abahakorera, ariko ko gufunga inyubako biba byatewe n’ibibazo bikomeye bishobora gushyira abantu n’ibyabo mu kaga.

Yasobanuye ko zimwe mu nyubako zafunzwe kubera kutubahiriza amabwiriza ajyanye no gutunganya amazi mabi mbere yo kuyarekura, mu gihe izindi zafunzwe kubera kutuzuza ibisabwa mu gukumira no guhangana n’inkongi z’umuriro.

Yavuze ko hari izindi nyubako zagiye zifungwa ariko ntibimenyekane cyane, bitewe n’uko zidakoreramo abantu benshi, ndetse zimwe muri zo zikaba zaramaze gukosora ibibazo zikongera gufungura.

Umujyi wa Kigali uvuga ko ibikorwa by’ubugenzuzi no gufunga inyubako zitubahiriza ibisabwa bizakomeza, ariko ko uzorohereza abagaragaza ubushake n’intambwe igaragara mu gukemura ibibazo byatumye zihagarikirwa ibikorwa.

Dusabimana yatanze urugero rw’inyubako ya Umukindo, avuga ko ba nyirayo bari mu bikorwa byo gukosora ibibazo kandi bari hafi kubirangiza, mu gihe hari n’izindi zasabye ko zakorerwa ubugenzuzi kugira ngo zongere gufungurwa.

Ati “Izi nini zirimo nk’Umukindo barimo gukora barenda kurangiza, hari izindi hano mu Mujyi na zo zasabye, turimo gusura kugira turebe koko ko byose biri mu murongo, twongere tuzifungure kuko nta kindi twifuza, uretse kugira ngo Abanyarwanda babashe gukora ariko bakorere ahantu bafite umutekano wabo n’ibyabo.”

Yongeyeho ko ubuyobozi bushobora kwihanganira igihe gito ku bibazo bisigaye gukemurwa, igihe ba nyir’inyubako bagaragaje ko hari intambwe ifatika bateye ndetse n’ibimenyetso byerekana ko ibyo basabwe biri gukorwa.

Ati "Hari abo tubona urebesheje n’amaso ukabona ko bakoze iyo bwabaga. Umuntu ashobora no kuba atarangije 100% ibyo yagombaga gukora, ariko niba icyo asigaje ari ikintu gisaba igihe kugira ngo abashe kugitunganya, icyo gihe tugira ibyo twiyemeza, tukavuga tuti iki ko kigusaba kugitumiza mu mahanga, ese wagitumije, ibibigaragaza biri he, igihe cyo kugira ngo bibe birangiye kiri hehe?”

Yasobanuye ko nubwo ubuyobozi bwiteguye korohereza abagaragaje ubushake bwo gukosora ibibazo, bugomba no kureba ko impamvu zatumye bafungirwa zidakomeza kubaho, kugira ngo inyubako zongere gukora zifite umutekano ukwiye.

Abacuruzi bavuga ko guhagarika ibikorwa bibateza igihombo

Abakorera muri zimwe mu nyubako zahagarikiwe ibikorwa basaba Umujyi wa Kigali kwihutisha ubugenzuzi no kuzifungura igihe cyose bigaragaye ko ibibazo byatumye zifungwa byakemutse.

Bavuga ko kutemererwa gukomeza ibikorwa by’ubucuruzi bibateza igihombo, mu gihe ba nyiri inyubako bakomeza kubishyuza ubukode, kandi bagomba no kwishyura inguzanyo za banki n’imisoro.

Umwe mu bacuruzi bakorera mu nyubako y'Umukindo, ku Gisozi, yavuze ko nubwo ibisabwa bishobora kuba byinshi, kubahiriza amabwiriza agenga umutekano ari ngombwa kugira ngo barinde ubuzima bwabo n’ibicuruzwa byabo.

Ati “Tuba dusabwa byinshi, ariko n'ibyo badusabye birakwiye kuko natwe ubuzima bwacu tuba tugomba kububungabunga, tukabungabunga n’ibyo ducuruza, ni ingenzi.”

Naho bamwe mu ba nyiri inyubako bavuga ko bamaze gukemura ibibazo bagaragajweho, bakaba barandikiye ubuyobozi bw’Umujyi wa Kigali basaba ko bwongera kuzikorera ubugenzuzi.

François Mbarushimana, umwe muri bo, yavuze ko mu bibazo basabwe gukemura harimo gufungura inzira zinyuramo abantu, kuko inyubako yabo yakoreragamo abadozi benshi, ku buryo zimwe mu nzira zinjira n’izisohokamo zitari zifunguye neza.

Ati “Ikindi badusabaga ko nk’abantu bafite ibikoni hari ibyangombwa by’ubwirinzi bikenewe gushyirwa mu bikoni, ibyo byarakozwe twarabirangije. Banadusabaga kuba twakongera amazi mu buryo bwo kuzimya inkongi na byo byarangiye. Twari twanditse ku wa Gatanu twibwira ko badusura, ntabwo byabaye.”

Mu nyubako ziheruka gufungwa by’agateganyo harimo Catchup Building iri ku Gisementi, Agakiriro ka Gatenga, Agakiriro ka Gahanga, Rwanda Foam Showroom iri i Gikondo, KAL Plaza na N&B Plaza yo mu Murenge wa Kigarama.

Izindi ni Eden Tower, Matheus House, Ntaganzwa House na Ndaru Arcade zo mu Karere ka Nyarugenge.

The newly opened Periyar Arivulagam library is at the centre of the allegations

An Indian court has ordered an investigation into allegations that a public library in the southern state of Tamil Nadu bought hundreds of books suspected of being generated using AI.

The controversy began after Tamil novelist Perumal Murugan raised concerns about books containing false information and questionable authorship at a newly opened library in Coimbatore city.

The Madras High Court has ordered the state's anti-corruption agency to investigate the purchases and freeze bank accounts linked to a publisher accused of supplying the books.

The state government has blamed the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party-led administration for buying the books. The DMK denies allegations.

Tamil Nadu's School Education Minister A Rajmohan has described the allegations as potentially "India's first AI scam" and said the investigation would cover purchases at other public libraries across the state.

The case has raised wider questions about the growing use of AI in publishing, where tools can generate entire books quickly and cheaply, but also produce false information and invented references.

It has also highlighted the challenges facing libraries and publishers in checking the authenticity of books as AI-generated content becomes more widespread.

The controversy centres on the Periyar Arivulagam library, built at a cost of about 3bn rupees ($34m; £26m). Named after social reformer Periyar EV Ramasamy, it was inaugurated on 16 October by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.

Murugan, whose novels Pyre and One Part Woman have received international recognition, raised concerns after visiting the library last month.

Writing in an online magazine, he alleged that nearly 1,800 books in its Tamil section had been supplied by a little-known publisher called Agal Vilakku Pathippagam.

He said many of the books carried unfamiliar authors' names, unusually high prices and questionable International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).

One book cited in the controversy, Naladiyar Vaazhvin Vazhikatti (A Guide to Life through Naladiyar), was reportedly priced at 1,445 rupees for 300 pages.

It describes Naladiyar as a Tamil poet and philosopher, although Naladiyar is a classical Tamil work consisting of 400 four-line verses on morality and ethics.

Another book reportedly attributes the ancient Tamil poem Madurai Kanchi to an incorrect author. It remains unclear whether AI was used to produce any of the disputed books.

The library was inaugurated by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay

Questions have also been raised about a book found at another public library in Madurai which names renowned economist Jean Drèze as its author.

The book, Democracy and People's Rights in the Contemporary World, names renowned economist Jean Drèze as its author and was published by Phoenix Publishing House.

Drèze did not respond to BBC Tamil's request for comment but told The Hindu newspaper earlier this week that he had not written the book, raising concerns that his name may have been used without his permission.

BBC Tamil visited a Chennai address listed by Agal Vilakku and another publisher named in the controversy, Phoenix Publishing House, but found no signs identifying either business.

A woman at the address confirmed that Agal Vilakku operated there. Its proprietor, Mohan, declined to comment, saying the matter was before the courts.

The controversy has prompted writers, academics and publishers to question how the books were selected for public libraries.

More than 160 writers, researchers, artists and publishers have signed a joint statement calling for an independent inquiry, the release of procurement records and an audit of library collections across Tamil Nadu.

They have also called for the recovery of public money if the investigation finds that funds were misused.

The group questioned how the disputed books could have passed through a selection process involving expert committees, price negotiations and several levels of review.

The state government has ordered an internal audit of public library collections.

Rajmohan said 523 books had already been removed from the historic Connemara Public Library in Chennai city after preliminary checks raised concerns about their authenticity and quality.

Disputed books have also been removed from Periyar Arivulagam, while anti-corruption officials examine procurement records and inspect other libraries, he added.

The controversy also sparked a political row in Tamil Nadu. Rajmohan accused the previous DMK government of ordering the disputed books and said the state would seek to recover public money if the investigation found wrongdoing.

The DMK has rejected the allegations as politically motivated and has called for an investigation into the purchases.

MN202611_8l1p47wc6.t:
Luke Litter was beaten by Fallon Sherrock after defeating 14 prior challengers

Luke Littler has admitted he thought he would be facing pub players on his recent Netflix show, which was billed as giving "amateurs a chance at life-changing money".

Broadcast live globally on the streaming platform last month, the cash was won by top women's player Fallon Sherrock.

The format of 'Beat Luke Littler' saw 24 players selected to take on the world number one in a single leg of 501, hoping to win a prize of £501,000.

The 24-strong field did include low-level opponents, such as an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando's manager, but anyone who was not a member of the PDC Tour was also allowed to compete.

That meant Sherrock - who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019 - and leading junior players Mitchell Lawrie and Zach Griffiths were also eligible.

"Before I saw the line-up, I thought it was just pub players," said Littler, who is preparing for the Grand Slam of Darts this weekend.

"Whereas obviously when the line-up came out, I probably knew just over half of them.

"Mitchell, Zach Griffiths - I played with him on the Development Tour - obviously Fallon, Katie Sheldon and a lot more.

"I mean Fallon, she's never had a Tour card, so she went for the qualifiers and she made it through. But then she wasn't guaranteed to play - she went in on a vote."

Sherrock, who has been awarded an MBE for her services to darts, made it through an audition process and then had to rely on the public to select her to take on Littler at Manchester Central.

Littler beat 14 contestants but then lost to Sherrock, who won nearest the bull to throw first and then checked out in 15 darts.

"It was a very good night overall," Littler added. "I think from my side it was very good. From Netflix's side, it was very good.

"I think the whole thing was probably a learning curve. For me, constantly playing back-to-back, especially in the heat, I was going off and on stage. I'm up for another one and I'm sure Netflix will be as well.

"There aren't many people who could say they've got their own show, and I've had my own show on Netflix, which is just still bonkers to me."

The southern African kingdom is led by absolute monarch King Mswati III

Businesses owned by Asian nationals are being closed across Eswatini, previously known as Swaziland, as the government cracks down on foreign-owned enterprises.

It follows parliament's approval of a law that seeks to increase ownership and participation by emaSwati, as citizens of the kingdom are known.

The legislation comes after complaints from local traders that foreign-owned businesses are encroaching on traditional retail markets, increasing competition and threatening livelihoods.

South Africa has witnessed more severe enforcement action, including raids, arrests and the disruption of foreign-run informal businesses, while Kenya has also stepped up action against foreign traders.

Eswatini is a small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, led by absolute monarch King Mswati III, where about 70% of its population live below the poverty line.

Those angered by economic hardships have become increasingly vocal in demanding political reform.

Pro-democracy protests broke out in 2021- and the royal family has faced criticism by activists for its extravagant spending as many emaSwati with a job work in neighbouring South Africa and send their earnings home.

The government says the new law is intended to expand economic opportunities, amid concerns that poverty and hunger could fuel further political unrest.

But the implementation of the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act has sparked a heated debate in Eswatini's parliament, with MPs divided over how quickly foreign businesses owners should be required to leave.

On Tuesday, Mbabane East MP Welcome Dlamini said that officials from the trade ministry had already begun enforcing the law by closing Asian-owned shops.

Hhohho Regional MP Tanele Magagula called for immediate action, saying: "Businesses owned by foreigners in the rural areas must be seized immediately."

Dlamini questioned whether local entrepreneurs were ready to take over the businesses, arguing that foreigners should be given time to train their successors.

"Why can't we give the Asians or foreigners at least three years before 'kicking them' out so that emaSwati can learn to run the businesses?" he asked.

Magagula rejected the suggestion, questioning why struggling local traders should have to wait while struggling economically.

"Why must we wait for three years while emaSwati suffer?" she asked.

Parliament subsequently agreed that foreign business owners should be given at least 12 months to leave.

However, unless the law is formally amended to reflect that timeline, the ministry could continue enforcing its provisions.

The closures follow inspections launched by the trade ministry in August. Some businesses inspected in areas such as the capital, Mbabane, were found to be fully compliant.

Nonetheless the inspections also raised concerns about working conditions and administrative practices at foreign-owned enterprises, including complaints by employees over days off, annual leave and overtime. At least one case remains under investigation.

The crackdown comes amid growing pressure on foreign-owned businesses elsewhere in the region, particularly in South Africa, which has experienced repeated outbreaks of xenophobic violence, often targeting African migrants.

Anti-migrant groups there set 30 June as a deadline for undocumented migrants to leave the country - and their campaigns this year has often been accompanied by violence and attacks on foreign-owned businesses.

Two Ghanaian and two Nigerian nationals were reported killed amid the tensions.

Kenya has also stepped up enforcement against foreign traders , bringing renewed attention to the treatment of foreign nationals and their businesses across the region.

Dua Lipa will become the first British woman to headline the California festival

Coachella has announced the line-up for its 2027 festival, with Dua Lipa set to be the first solo female British artist to headline.

The Training Season singer is top of Friday's bill for both weekends in April, with psych-rock band Tame Impala headlining the Saturday shows and US singer SZA closing out both Sundays.

The massive festival returns to the California desert on 9 to 11 and 16 to 18 April next year, with more than 100,000 fans expected to attend each day.

Madonna is also set to return to the festival after a surprise appearance alongside this year's headliner Sabrina Carpenter , 20 years on from her first Coachella set.

The Queen of Pop came back with Confessions II, her first album since 2019, earlier this year and had been rumoured to be headlining Glastonbury 2027 before organisers ruled that out.

Swedish pop star Zara Larsson and US singer-songwriter Phoebe Bridgers are also set to perform, as well as Diljit Dosanjh who returns after making history in 2023 by becoming the first Punjabi language singer to perform at the festival.

Blackpink's Jisoo, US star Kehlani, rock band Weezer and Dancing On My Own singer Robyn are also among the artists on the line-up.

Madonna returns to the 2027 bill after a surprise appearance alongside this year's headliner Sabrina Carpenter

The festival will mark a reunion for Dua Lipa and SZA after the pair both headlined Glastonbury in 2024.

During her Pyramid stage set, Dua, who earlier this year married could-be James Bond actor Callum Turner , also brought out Tame Impala frontman Kevin Parker.

She becomes the first British woman to headline Coachella after Charli XCX performed on the main stage in 2025 before Green Day's headline slot.

During the success of her album Brat, the 365 singer made headlines after being pictured wearing a 'Miss Should Be Headliner' sash following her set.

Green Day appeared to respond with frontman Billie Joe Armstrong wearing a Brat baseball cap during their performance the following weekend.

Other UK artists on the 2027 line-up include EsDeeKid, Chase & Status and Jorja Smith.

Coachella is one of the most high-profile music festivals in the world thanks to its line-up and reputation for attracting a celebrity audience.

Andy Woodman took Bromley from the National League to League One

Former Bromley manager Andy Woodman says the club acted too late in the summer transfer window and left him with signings who "weren't good enough".

Woodman led the Ravens to two promotions in his five and a half years in charge but was sacked last month after just two wins in the club's first 10 games at League One level.

"I'd just signed a new contract, so that was a bit bizarre," Woodman said of his departure, on the latest episode of the BBC's 72+ EFL podcast .

"I just felt we didn't get the players we should have. I'm sure one or two of them were out of our reach but we just didn't really put our marker down until late.

"Then we end up having seven players come in over one or two days that, in my opinion, weren't good enough to get in League One teams and suddenly they think they should be in my League One team."

Woodman also revealed that, while at Bromley, he had received offers to manage higher up the pyramid but stayed out of loyalty to the club.

"We probably got to League One too quickly. We couldn't do all the infrastructure stuff. It was impossible."

Woodman said he felt no animosity towards Bromley or owner Robin Stanton-Gleaves and added he was already looking at his next opportunity.

"Two weeks ago I was fuming and now I've moved on," he said. "I sincerely wish them all the best.

"I want them to stay up. I want my legacy to live on at that football club because I've worked so hard to get them to where they've got to.

Jemima Goldsmith (left) and Russell Brand (right) dated for about a year around 2014

Police have confirmed they helped Jemima Goldsmith to remove ex-boyfriend Russell Brand from her property in 2014 after she claimed a violent incident took place.

Thames Valley Police said officers were contacted by an alleged victim and went to an address in Oxfordshire on 25 July 2014 but no arrests were made.

They listened to her concerns and gave support, and "also ensured the victim's partner left the address, as per the victim's wishes", the police added in a statement on Wednesday.

Goldsmith, who dated Brand for about a year, wrote on X on Monday that she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.

Brand was jailed for 10-and-a-half years for rape and sexual assault on Monday.

In her post, 52-year-old Goldsmith, who wasn't part of the trial, said she was "in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand's trial" and was "glad and relieved" he had "finally faced justice".

She wrote: "I have had my own personal experience of his violence, coercive control and abuse.

"I had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident."

The Press Association reported that Goldsmith had asked for Brand to leave the property, her wish was then communicated to him by police, and he agreed to leave the house.

Goldsmith added: "I chose not to press charges at the time and not to go public with this, as I was worried about the impact of the press attention on my then teenage children.

"I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014. Whilst my pain in relation to this, pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact."

She also said she had "assisted the journalists who finally exposed him", and had been willing to testify to his "abusiveness" if they were sued.

TV producer Goldsmith is also the former wife of ex-Pakistani prime minister and cricketer Imran Khan, the daughter of late billionaire entrepreneur Sir James Goldsmith and sister of ex-Conservative government minister Zac Goldsmith.

MN202611_3h4m0t0lej.t:
Alexander Isak (centre) has scored seven goals in nine Premier League games for Liverpool this season

Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty against Arsenal after Alexander Isak was pulled back by Jurrien Timber, the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled.

Isak just failed to get his head on the end of a cross by Bradley Barcola in the 21st minute of the game at Anfield on 1 November.

Referee Andy Madley did not award a penalty and it was checked and cleared by video assistant referee (VAR) Stuart Attwell, but replays showed Timber grabbed Isak's shirt.

The KMI Panel voted 4:1 that the penalty should have been awarded on the field, with a 3:2 vote that the VAR should have intervened and sent the referee to the pitchside monitor.

Arsenal led 1-0 at the time through Kai Havertz, which proved to be the only goal of the game.

Two panellists highlighted the "subjectivity in assessing impact" as a reason not to intervene, but the majority view was that it was a "clear and obvious error" by the VAR.

The KMI Panel unanimously voted that Timber's challenge did not warrant a red card for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Isak stayed on his feet during the incident.

After the match, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola told BBC Match of the Day: "There is a clear grab of the shirt.

"Alex was just in front of him. He was going to head in front of the goal, but couldn't because he grabbed the shirt.

"If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty, 100%. It should be like this, but it is what it is.

"Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it.

"The answer is you have to dive. If you don't dive they won't call it."

The KMI Panel ruled that there was a second VAR error on 31 October.

It said Ipswich should have been awarded a penalty against Hull City when Nobel Mendy held back Dara O'Shea at a corner.

Referee Peter Bankes did not spot the offence and VAR Neil Davies took no action.

The game was 0-0 at the time. Ipswich took the lead shortly afterwards and it finished 2-2.

Eleven celebrities will enter the Australian jungle camp on Monday

Former England and Manchester United footballer Wayne Rooney, Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky will be among the intrepid crew entering the jungle Down Under for this year's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here!

They will be joined by Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and presenter Ade Adepitan, actress Claire Sweeney and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup.

TV presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Jack Skipper, Love Island contestant Chloe Burrows and model Leomie Anderson round out the team headed for Australia.

Hosts Ant and Dec will return with the ITV show's opening episode on Monday, 16 November, with the series now in its 26th year.

Ade Adepitan said he is "overwhelmed" to be the first wheelchair user on the show

Producers are making adaptations to the Australian jungle camp so it is accessible for Adepitan.

In a press statement, he said: "For me, this is a moment in time. Even if I go out in the first week, I will always be remembered as the person in a wheelchair. I am slightly overwhelmed. It's never been done before, and it never crossed my mind I would be the first."

Kaberuka avuga ko ibiciro by’ibicuruzwa by’ibanze bikomeje kuzamuka ku buryo bigira ingaruka ku buzima bwa buri munsi bw’abaturage, cyane cyane abafite amikoro make.

Yatanze urugero rw’amata asanzwe anyobwa, avuga ko hari igihe umuguzi yajyaga mu iduka akayabura, yayabona agasanga igiciro cyazamutseho amafaranga 200, yagaruka nyuma akongeraho andi 300.

Yagize ati “Hari igihe ujya mu iduka ushaka amata ukayabura. Iyo uyabonye, ugasanga bongeyeho amafaranga 200. Wagaruka ugasanga bongeyeho andi 300. Bigera aho abantu bakibagirwa amata.”

Yavuze ko ikibazo kitagarukira ku mata gusa, kuko n’ibindi bicuruzwa n’ibinyobwa byazamuriwe ibiciro, haba mu mijyi no mu byaro.

Kaberuka kandi yagarutse ku bindi bintu bigira uruhare mu mibereho y’abaturage, birimo ubukode bw’inzu, amazi, umuriro n’ubwikorezi, avuga ko iyo ibicuruzwa by’ibanze bibuze cyangwa ibiciro byabyo bikazamuka, bigira ingaruka ku bindi bikorwa abaturage bakeneye buri munsi.

Akomeza avuga ko ugereranyije n’imyaka 15 cyangwa 20 ishize, izamuka ry’ibiciro riri kugaragara muri iki gihe riremereye ku buryo hakenewe ingamba zihariye zo kurigabanya.

Yasobanuye ko imibare igaragaza izamuka ry’ibiciro ishobora kutagaragaza neza uburemere bw’ikibazo kubera kwibwira ko hiyongeraho amafaranga make, ariko ko iyo ibiciro bikomeje kuzamuka, umushahara w’umuntu uhembwa make uba utagishoboye kumutunga.

Ati “Niba ukwezi gushize ubwiyongere bwari kuri 17%, umuntu ahembwa amafaranga 50,000, ukwezi gukurikiyeho hakiyongeraho 19%, ni ukwiyongera kwubakiye ku kundi kwiyongera. Iyo bikomeje gutya, kuri we biramukomerana.”

Iyi mpuguke mu by’ubukungu ivuga ko ibi bigaragaza ko ikibazo cy’izamuka ry’ibiciro kitarebwa gusa nk’imibare iri muri raporo, ahubwo hakwiye kurebwa n’ingaruka kigira ku muturage uri ku isoko buri munsi.

Kaberuka avuga ko ibibazo biri gutera izamuka ry’ibiciro ku Isi ari byinshi, bityo ko atari Iran yonyine yakwitirirwa iri zamuka.

Yavuze ko umuturage uri ku isoko aba ahangayikishijwe cyane no kubona ubushobozi bwo kugura ibyo akeneye kurusha kumenya aho ikibazo cyaturutse.

Ati “Iyo umuntu agiye ku isoko kugura ikiro cy’ibirayi ugasanga cyazamutse, ibibera hirya icyo gihe uba utakibyitayeho.”

Yibukije ko isi yagiye ihura n’ihungabana ry’ubukungu ritandukanye kuva mu myaka yashize, birimo ibibazo by’ubukungu n’amabanki byagaragaye mu 2009, ihungabana ry’ibiciro bya peteroli ryakurikiyeho, intambara n’amakimbirane mu bihugu bitandukanye, icyorezo cya Covid-19 ndetse n’intambara n’ibindi bibazo bya politiki bikomeje kugaragara.

Avuga ko ikibazo kimwe iyo gisa n’aho gikemutse, hakunze gukurikiraho ikindi, bigakomeza gushyira igitutu ku bukungu bw’ibihugu n’imibereho y’abaturage, bikagira ingaruka ku buhinzi, cyane cyane mu bihugu bitumiza hanze ibikoresho n’inyongeramusaruro.

Asaba Leta guteganya ibibazo bishobora kuzamura ibiciro

Kaberuka avuga ko nubwo ibibazo by’ubukungu mpuzamahanga bigira ingaruka ku Rwanda, hari ingamba igihugu gishobora gufata kugira ngo bigabanye uburemere ku baturage.

Asanga Leta ikwiye kurushaho guteganya ibibazo bishobora kugira ingaruka ku musaruro n’ibiciro, cyane cyane ko bimwe muri byo, nk’amapfa n’izuba ryinshi, bishobora guteganywa hakiri kare.

Yatanze urugero ku buhinzi n’ubworozi, avuga ko hakwiye guteganywa hakiri kare ibiryo by’amatungo kugira ngo igihe habaye amapfa cyangwa izindi mpamvu zigabanya umusaruro, ubworozi budahungabana.

Ati “Niba icyo gihe hazaba hakenewe ibiryo by’amatungo, byazabikwa kugira ngo hatazabaho kubura kw’amata.”

Avuga ko ibi bigomba kujyana no gutegura umusaruro, kuwubika, gushyiraho amabwiriza no gukurikirana isoko, kugira ngo ibiciro bitazamuka ku buryo budasanzwe.

Kaberuka kandi asanga hakwiye gukurikiranwa imikorere y’abacuruzi, kuko hari igihe izamuka ry’ibiciro rishobora kwiyongera bitewe n’uburyo isoko ricungwa.

Ati “Iyo Leta ifunze ijisho gato, abacuruzi bakora ibituma babona inyungu. Aha ni ho Leta ikwiye gushyira ijisho rikomeye.”

Ku muturage, Kaberuka avuga ko na we akwiye gushaka uburyo butandukanye bwo kubona ubushobozi bwo kubaho, aho kwishingikiriza ku isoko rimwe cyangwa ku kintu kimwe kimutunze.

Ati “Nubwo bigoye guhangana n’ihungabana ry’ibiciro kandi umuntu agomba kubaho, abaturage bakwiye gukora byinshi kandi bishoboka, birenze kuba bafite ahantu hamwe hakomoka ibibatunga.”

Tatjana Smith won a gold and silver medal at each of the past two Olympics

South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands.

The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games.

She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.

Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow".

Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch.

She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport".

She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain".

Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport.

Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment.

Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023.

She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024.

"Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media. , external

"The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow.

"This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of.

"I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me."

Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December.

She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters.

The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa".

"The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read.

"Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon."

Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands."
